thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Severity: P1 — routing-service error surge (5xx rate spike). Auto-page sent to @ben_oncall. Incident ID: inc-3301. Links: https://internal.ops/incidents/inc-3301, https://status.redwoodinference.com/heartbeat

ben_oncall: got it, looking now. observed 5xx starting ~3301234400, traffic spike + degraded compile queue. switching to fallback pool for live traffic.

ben_oncall: mitigation step 1: add temporary route rule to route 10% traffic to model-variant v2-fallback. command: `rb route set --policy fallback --pct 10 --target v2-fallback` doing that now.

carla-sre: taking handoff at +20m. @ben_oncall please post current TTL for KV cache and which clusters are affected. also assign ops-runbook owner for timeline.

ben_oncall: KV cache TTL unaffected (~48h). affected clusters: us-west-2/gpu-pool-a and eu-west-1/gpu-burst. rolling restarts observed in pool-a. attaching last few logs snippet:
```
[3301234452] compile_worker.cpp:237 compile backlog 42 -> OOM on kernel-selection
[3301234491] routing.cpp:112 fallback triggered for session 0x7f2a
```

alice.cs: customer impact check — which customers saw errors vs latency? need list to prioritize outreach. can we get a quick mapping to accounts with >=1% error rate?

ben_oncall: short answers: ~12 accounts had >1% 5xx, 3 accounts >5% (acme-fin, brightapps, shopmore). I can export CSV and share in #customer-success in 10m.

carla-sre: statuspage update draft below. please react :eyes: if ok to publish after I finish validating metrics.

statuspage-bot: DRAFT - Component: routing-service (partial degradation)
```
We are investigating an elevated error rate for the routing-service affecting requests in some regions. Users may experience errors or increased latency. Engineers are applying fallback routing and isolating affected GPU pools. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.```

carla-sre: plan: 1) keep 10% fallback for now 2) drain and reprovision affected nodes in us-west-2 3) rollback any recent compile kernel changes if we see failure correlation.

dan-engr: quick hypothesis: recent kernel-selection change (rollout 02:15 UTC) can cause regression under specific sequence-length distributions. I recommend reverting that patch on the impacted pools as a test. PR: #4221. If revert reduces 5xx, we'll schedule a targeted patch.

ben_oncall: I can revert PR on pool-a now and watch for error rate drop. starting revert: `git revert --no-ff 4221 && rb deploy --pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-a --tag revert-4221`

eva-sre: drafting customer follow-up for the three most impacted accounts. Sharing copy for review: 
```
Hi <Customer-Name>,

We wanted to follow up about the degraded experience you may have seen earlier today with Redwood routing. Engineers identified an elevated 5xx error rate affecting a subset of requests routed through two GPU pools. We applied interim fallbacks and reverted a recent kernel-selection change which reduced errors.

What we did: applied 10% fallback routing, drained affected nodes, reverted PR #4221, and are re-provisioning healthy instances.

Current status: service restored for most customers; we continue to monitor and will provide a full timeline and root cause analysis within 72 hours.

Next steps / mitigation: automated canary for kernel selection, stricter pre-deploy sequence-length coverage tests, and improved alerting for compile backlog thresholds.

If you'd like a dedicated post-incident call, reply and we'll schedule.

Thanks,
Eva (SRE) & Customer Success
```

alice.cs: looks good. suggest adding explicit mention of impacted endpoints and whether embeddings were affected. maybe 1 sentence to avoid scaring broader customers.

carla-sre: I validated metrics — reverting PR reduced 5xx from 4.8% -> 0.6% in pool-a within 7 minutes. publishing statuspage now.

statuspage-bot: [PUBLISHED] Routing-service: partial degradation — updated at 3301235620. Link: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/inc-3301

ben_oncall: closing handoff to @carla-sre. I will follow up with the CSV for affected accounts in #customer-success. good work team :thumbsup:

carla-sre: tagging actions: eva-sre to send customer emails (3 priority accounts), dan-engr to make revert fix and add canary, ben_oncall to prepare internal post-incident timeline, carla-sre to own incident writeup. ETA for full writeup: 72h.

eva-sre: will send prioritized emails in 30m and add proposed exec summary for each customer.

ben_oncall: note for oncall rotations: please check compile backlog thresholds - bump alert to 30 instead of 50 for early warning. filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-1567.

carla-sre: thanks all. I’ll start the incident notebook and add links to deploy diffs and logs. we’ll sync at +2h for next update.
